{{Short description|Sino-Tibetan language spoken in China}} {{for|Bangni dialect of Arunachal Pradesh in India|Na dialect}} {{Distinguish|Dorerin Naoero}} {{Infobox language |name=Na |altname=Narua |nativename= |pronunciation= |states=[[China]] |region=[[Sichuan]] |ethnicity=[[Mosuo]] |speakers= 47,000 |date= 2010 |ref= e24 |familycolor=Sino-Tibetan |fam2=[[Lolo-Burmese languages|Lolo-Burmese]] or [[Qiangic languages|Qiangic]] |fam3=[[Naic languages|Naic]] |fam4=[[Naish languages|Naish]] |iso3=nru |glotto=yong1270 |glottorefname=Narua }} '''Na''' (or '''Narua''', '''Mosuo''') is a language of the [[Naish languages|Naish]] subbranch of the [[Naic languages|Naic]] group of the [[Sino-Tibetan languages]]. ==Varieties== '''Yongning Na''', which is spoken in [[Yongning Township, Ninglang County|Yongning Township]], [[Ninglang Yi Autonomous County|Ninglang County]], [[Lijiang]], [[Yunnan]], [[China]], has been documented by Jacques and Michaud (2011).Jacques, Guillaume, and Alexis Michaud. 2011. "[http://halshs.archives-ouvertes.fr/halshs-00537990/ Approaching the historical phonology of three highly eroded Sino-Tibetan languages]." ''Diachronica'' 28:468-498. It has three tonal levels.{{Cite book |last=Michaud |first=Alexis |url=https://langsci-press.org/catalog/book/109 |title=Tone in Yongning Na: Lexical tones and morphotonology |date=2017 |publisher=Language Science Press |isbn=978-3-946234-87-6 |series=Studies in Diversity Linguistics |location=Berlin}} A trilingual dictionary is available online.{{Cite book |last=Michaud |first=Alexis |url=https://shs.hal.science/halshs-01204638/ |title=Na (Mosuo) – English – Chinese dictionary |last2=Latami |first2=Dashilamu |last3=Milan |first3=Pascale-Marie |last4=Galliot |first4=Benjamin |publisher=Lexica |year=2025 |edition=version 2.1 |location=France |language=en}} '''Lataddi Narua''' is notable for having only two [[Tone (linguistics)|tonal]] levels.Dobbs, Roselle, and La Mingqing. 2016 "The two-level tonal system of Lataddi Narua."
